title: Replace a bakery's paper notebook with an invoicing app
summary: A developer had Claude Code interview him, plan and build a count, delivery and invoice app for his wife's four-cafe bakery in about 20 hours.
agent_role: Claude Code interviewed the author to write scope, plan and spec documents, then built the app in 8 checked slices, listing its own judgment calls for approval. The author directed, tested and decided; a second Claude chat wrote prompts and reviewed the code.
outcome: Author reports a working app in about 20 hours; planning caught a time-zone invoice bug and price-change issue before coding.
what_they_did: The author's wife ran her bakery from one paper notebook of shelf counts and invoices. He used Claude Code with a skill pack that interviewed him one question at a time. It wrote the scope, plan and spec, which he approved. It then built the app in 8 small checked slices: count, deliver, branded invoice, and a ledger of who owes what.
how_it_went: He says the interview caught a server clock that would misdate evening invoices and a pricing link that would rewrite old invoices. Each slice ended with 'calls I made that you should check.' A hand-timed run still found a wrong assumption in the plan.
worth_knowing: Keeping decisions in plan files let him start fresh chats without losing context. Only real use caught the one wrong guess the plan carried to the end.
prompt: I want an app for my [type of small business] to replace [current paper process]. Interview me one question at a time, then write a scope document, a screen-by-screen plan and a technical spec. Wait for my approval on each. Build it in small slices, and end each slice with a list of decisions you made that I should check. Store money in whole cents and dates in [your time zone]. Ask before deploying or sending any emails.

curation.rationale: A real small-business tool with code, demo video and a clear look at how the agent interviewed, planned and flagged its own decisions.
